draft.title: Justifying a personal response
card: A personal response is your own reaction to a text, such as feeling sad, tense or amused. A strong one does not stop at the feeling.
It explains why the text caused that reaction. To do this, point to how the text was made: its tone, a character's voice, the genre, or the language used.
Weak: "I felt scared when I read it." Stronger: "The short, flat sentences made the danger feel close, so I felt scared."
A good pattern is to name your reaction, name the feature of the text, then link the two. Short quoted words or a described moment can back up your point.
draft.remember: Say how you felt, then show which part of the text made you feel it.

a.q: Which sentence best justifies a personal response to a short story?
opts: The narrator's joking voice made the sad ending hit harder
I really loved this story and everyone should read it
The story made me feel sad because sad things happen in it
I felt very sad at the end, and I cried when I finished it
a.why: The right answer links a feeling to a feature of the text, the narrator's voice. The tempting option about crying only states how strong the feeling was and does not say what in the text caused it.
a.clue: Look for the sentence that names something the writer did.

b.q: Tom writes: "The poem made me feel hopeful." He wants to justify this response. Which addition would help most?
opts: The bright sunrise images and steady rhythm lifted the mood
I often feel hopeful when I read poems, as I did this time
The poem is short, so it was easy to read and I felt hopeful
Many students in my class also felt hopeful after reading it
b.why: The first option explains how the poet's imagery and rhythm created the hopeful feeling, which is the job of a justification. The option about other students repeats the feeling and adds no reason from the text.
b.clue: Which option points to how the poem was made?
